newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to destroy another 40,000 swine-fever pigs.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to destroy another 40,000 swine-fever pigs.

text.p: Belgium plans to slaughter and destroy another 40,000 pigs which might be infected by swine fever, Agriculture Minister Karel Pinxten said on Monday.
The new campaign, which will last two weeks, will take the total number of pigs slaughtered to 56,500.
Belgium -- which has about seven million pigs -- has already slaughtered 16,500 pigs from 18 farms following an outbreak of swine fever in the northeast of the country at the end of June.
The 40,000 pigs to be slaughtered are from 40 farms which had been in contact with the farm in Bocholt, north-eastern Belgium, where the first outbreak was signalled last month.
Pinxten told a news conference he was not sure the outbreak had been caused by imported Dutch pigs, as some media reported.
"For the most recent case, I am sure there is no link with transports of pigs from Netherlands. For the other centres of swine fever, we are not sure," he said.
Most of the affected farms are in the provinces of Limburg and Liege, close to the Dutch and German borders.

In the most affected provinces all transport of pigs is forbidded. In other parts of Belgium it is forbidden to bring together pigs from several farms. All pig farms in the country must be checked by a veterinary every week.
